evidence.claim: Average administrative labor contrasts are near zero under the study design while occupational mobility changes. This does not identify zero productivity, a current global effect, or a physical-worker payroll coefficient.
evidence.locator: Sections 3.1–3.4; Figures 5–8; Appendix F; administrative outcomes through December 2024
evidence.methods: Adopter/non-adopter differential changes under counterfactual trend assumptions. Pooled worker earnings controls adopter-specific trends; dynamic estimates have different precision. Workplace treatment is reported encouraged use. Occupational mobility uses FTE hours in the latest occupation, not simply a worker switch count.
evidence.positive_finding: Occupational mobility is a measured changing margin; selection into adoption versus transition facilitation remains a competing interpretation. Absence of average earnings change does not erase this result.
evidence.limitations: Exact personal adoption timing is unobserved. Common effects on non-adopters are differenced out; the authors assess spillovers using additional evidence and a model, which does not make a global effect directly identified. Recorded hours are administrative labor input, not task-level active-time logs. Firm financial data stop in 2022; this audit establishes no causal revenue, margin or whole-service productivity effect. Occupational subgroups have wider intervals.

benchmarks.systems: GPT-4, Eureka, reward-aware physics prior and RL-trained policies.

analogies.mechanism: Training input allocation improves a bounded capability before integration and operation determine value.
analogies.source: Text-model pretraining loss under fixed training FLOPs
material_differences: Physical validation, embodiment and real-time control
Training loss differs from accepted output
analogies.prediction: Held-out site performance improves only when added data covers relevant failures and policy can exploit it.
analogies.falsifier: Added low-diversity data or extra model compute fails to reduce target-site intervention burden.
alternative_explanations: Data curation and optimizer improvements rather than scale

analogies.mechanism: Digital replication can scale quickly once infrastructure exists; physical rollout remains constrained by manufactured and supported assets.
required_similarities: Available compatible inputs and operational support
material_differences: Robot units, site adaptation, spares and depreciation
analogies.prediction: Installation/support capacity can bind after technically capable policies exist.
analogies.falsifier: Target evidence establishes negligible site/support work with qualified supply slack across representative expansion.

analogies.mechanism: Model accessibility can increase integration value, but platform integration can also absorb complements.
analogies.source: DeployCo/Ode implementation businesses and cloud-model relationships
required_similarities: Customer can contract for measurable output
analogies.prediction: Integrator advantage depends on lower repeat deployment cost or superior retained operating output.
analogies.falsifier: OEM bundles remove independent integrator margins or interfaces eliminate costly adaptation.

analogies.mechanism: Deployment access provides learning only through usable observations, access rights, selection and validated feedback.
analogies.source: QJE experience/learning heterogeneity and Census breadth
material_differences: Failed episodes not equivalent to expert demonstrations
analogies.prediction: Novel, usable exposure predicts held-out improvement better than raw installed robot count.
analogies.falsifier: More deployments create redundant/low-quality data, inaccessible rights or no target improvement.

analogies.mechanism: Benchmark improvements need acceptance, workflow and intervention accounting before economic interpretation.
analogies.target: Robotic control benchmarks to productive service
analogies.prediction: Adding walltime/retry/quality constraints changes cost per accepted output and sometimes ranking.
analogies.falsifier: Representative target operating trials show benchmark rank and economics remain stable under complete boundaries.
alternative_explanations: Harness differences rather than model capability

analogies.mechanism: Coordination improves decomposable work but incurs message, state and verification costs.
material_differences: Physical congestion and correlated hardware failure
analogies.prediction: Extra agents help independent diagnosis/planning more than tightly sequential transaction/control loops.
analogies.falsifier: Controlled target trials show no net gain after supervision and coordination resources or simple rule/solver matches performance.

analogies.prediction: An entrant must fund enterprise ramp beyond robot financing and beat same-technology incumbent.
analogies.falsifier: Funding exhaustion or incumbent digital adoption removes lead before positive cumulative cashflow.
alternative_explanations: Partner distribution rather than technology advantage

direct_contributions.digital_input: Images, a language objective, robot proprioception, descriptions of available policies, and history.
direct_contributions.output: A proposed task/policy selection or validated end-effector targets.
direct_contributions.interface: VLM scene description → LLM proposal and affordance filtering → scripted, learned or teleoperated policy. Astranomy's host validates the action.
direct_contributions.execution: A low-level robot controller is separate from the language planner. AutoRT is physical; Astranomy is simulated.
direct_contributions.timing: Autonomous collection is not productive throughput. Astranomy pauses simulation during inference.
direct_contributions.authority: Supervisors and guardrails retain operating authority; a model proposal does not prove success.
direct_contributions.acknowledgement: Measured state, episode outcomes and task-progress feedback.
direct_contributions.fallback: Reject unsupported tasks and stop or escalate to a human; recovery is not assumed perfect.
direct_contributions.comparator: The same embedded policy/controller without the additional reasoning layer, or simpler policy-selection rules.
direct_contributions.observed_effect: Diverse physical data collection in AutoRT; simulated manipulation success in Astranomy.
direct_contributions.missing_reason: No matched commercial-output, staffing and cost experiment.
direct_contributions.resources: Inference, time, teleoperator availability, reset work and safety monitoring.
direct_contributions.model_implication: Separate planning latency, inference cost, intervention probability and quality. Hold mandatory embedded software fixed across the robot row.

direct_contributions.digital_input: ERP orders and priorities; WMS/MES and inventory state; robot poses/routes; building state; staff capacity.
direct_contributions.output: A candidate allocation, route, schedule, work order or business transaction.
direct_contributions.interface: ERP/WMS/MES decision layer → validated task API → fleet manager → robot. Open-RMF messages include fleet_states, destination_requests, mode_requests, path_requests, DoorState and DoorRequest.
direct_contributions.execution: Conventional fleet traffic/building control is documented; SAP agents are announced. A combined LLM-to-robot production stack is not observed in these sources.
direct_contributions.timing: State freshness, deadlines, queues and confirmation latency must be explicit.
direct_contributions.authority: The customer process owner approves policy; the fleet manager controls robots. A read-only fleet cannot be commanded. Transaction permissions are not inferred.
direct_contributions.acknowledgement: Task acceptance/rejection, mission state, door state and inventory/work-order reconciliation.
direct_contributions.fallback: Idempotent transactions, timeouts, replanning and a human exception queue are proposed design requirements.
direct_contributions.comparator: Human dispatch with feasible conventional proximity/priority rules or a solver, matched information, authority and service obligations. H-PROXIMITY-2025 supplies a bounded implementation example, not a target coefficient.
direct_contributions.observed_effect: Interface feasibility and operator workflow limits; no isolated LLM productivity uplift. A conventional EMR intervention has adjusted observational timing associations; no payroll or clinical equivalence is established.
direct_contributions.missing_reason: No integrated production experiment isolates the LLM contribution.
direct_contributions.resources: Integration engineering, human supervision, inference, network and shared corridors/lifts.
direct_contributions.model_implication: Add control-rights and integration-readiness gates. Coordination can hurt performance. Separate urgent and nonurgent hospital cohorts.
direct_contributions.labor_measurement_contract: Join proposed digital coordination to actual accepted work, retained/new duties, a feasible paid staffing decision and every payer; individual time expectations are insufficient.

direct_contributions.authority: Engineers accept candidates and validation results; automatic production deployment is not implied.

direct_contributions.fallback: Discard unsafe or ineffective candidates, retain the baseline, or redesign with human input.

conventional_baselines.label: A stronger human-dispatch baseline
conventional_baselines.summary: A conventional proximity rule raises the empirical hurdle for robot or agent coordination. Compare the improved human service under the same due requests, capacity, acceptance and cost boundary.
conventional_baselines.source_boundary: Patient transport at one hospital in 2021–23, not medication delivery or a current target configuration. Adjusted associations and unadjusted outcomes answer different questions.
conventional_baselines.interpretation: The adjusted timing association can motivate local conventional-dispatch qualification. It cannot establish removed labor, clinical equivalence, a stronger result than a robot comparator, or the incremental value of an LLM.
conventional_baselines.uncertainty: Elapsed-time confidence interval: Table 2 [0.919,0.982]; narrative [0.915,0.982], unresolved. Table 3 is a group-interaction specification. No target coefficient or silently corrected result.

gates.requirement: Track every due request, cancellations, deadline misses and affected groups. A better average cannot establish acceptable service for each mandatory cohort.
Measure staff busy time, simultaneous tasks, retained coverage and paid schedules. Aggregate request elapsed time includes waiting and is not payroll.
Give the human dispatcher the same available state and authority. Assess model proposals only after conventional implementation, verification and recovery costs.
Qualify the actual patient or material workflow separately. Preserve custody, urgency, staffing and support; do not copy this study’s percentages.

labor_outcome_audits.finding: Table E.3 allocation figures condition on reported savings and the questionnaire asks expectations. Administrative labor contrasts and changing occupational mobility use a different measurement design.

rows.boundary: Table 1/B.1; do not reuse this count for Table E.3 allocation.

gates.requirement: Measure active human work, queues, retries and accepted output separately; a reported saving is a candidate mechanism.
Identify who receives released capacity, actual demand and deadlines, plus new review, integration and exception work; include non-users.
Reconcile schedules, wage bills, overtime, vacancies, agency labor and contractor invoices before and after a feasible staffing decision.
Hold complete timely service and quality fixed against competent human/conventional operation; incomplete work cannot finance a savings claim.
Assign integration, supervision, fallback and ramp obligations to the actual legal payer; customer payroll reduction may move work to a provider.
Separate adoption selection, demand and organizational changes from treatment; test target conditions before numerical transfer or entry valuation.
